verdict.rationale: Decagon documents configurable guardrails, natural-language AOPs that define agent behavior like SOPs, and integrations that handle escalations, which together imply a team could route topics to humans. Nothing explicitly documents marking topics as human-only or guaranteeing the agent will not answer them. Watchtower's post-hoc flagging is monitoring, not prevention, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: an explicit topic-level human-only or forced-handoff control, documentation of hard enforcement so the agent never freelances, examples covering legal, cancellation and security topics, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a support ops lead, I mark topics as human-only — legal threats, cancellations, security — and the agent never freelances on them

citations.quote: technical teams retain full visibility and control over guardrails
you can define agent behavior in natural language, the same way you train human agents with SOPs
handle escalations smoothly across chat, email, and voice channels
